4.text: people. Besides this, however, they seem to feel a dull aversion to marrying

5.text: and having a family. “It is more convenient thus,” was the answer of every

6.text: one of them to all my questions: “the more children, the more care.”

7.text: Marriages among the Reindeer Chukchee, as will be shown further on,

8.text: are concluded at every age, from very tender infancy up to the full-grown

9.text: adult. Their ideal of a bride includes, in the first place, physical strength

10.text: and ability to work. Even in their descriptions of womanly beauty, strength

11.text: of body is mentioned before everything else, and all other characteristics are

12.text: so combined as to make still more impressive the idea of greath strength.¹

13.text: Chastity of Women. — Chastity is not considered as in any way an

14.text: essential quality of an ideal bride. Indeed, the Chukchee language has no

15.text: word to express this idea, not even a special word for “girl.” It has only

16.text: the word ñeˊus˙qät (“woman”); in combination, also -ñew, -ñaw, -ñe, -ña.

17.text: Yaˊnřa-ñaw (“separate woman”) is used for any woman who, for the time being,

18.text: has no husband, whether she be a girl, a widow, or a divorced woman. For

19.text: “chastity” only a paraphrase may be used; such as, yep ayaaˊkᴇlên (“not yet

23.text: concerning sexual life. The people enjoy ribald tales and lewd gestures.

24.text: Many of the nick-names are very obscene.¹

25.text: In a tale about Aˊñqalo’s wife, when the young bride is brought to the

26.text: camp in a covered sledge, the neighbors say, “Let us have a look at this

27.text: young woman, Añqalo’s wife’s daughter.” — “No, it is impossible,” says the

28.text: bridegroom. “If you look at her, you will die!” They come to the place.

29.text: People gather from all sides, — old women with staffs, elderly people, the

30.text: middle-aged, young men. The old people say, “Let us have, though, but

31.text: one look!” — “Nay, if you look at her, you will die.” — “No, no! Are we

32.text: children? Are we foolish people? Make her appear. Let us have a look

33.text: at the female beauty.” — “As you like.” He told his wife to show from the

34.text: covered sledge only one of her hands. When they saw that hand, the old

35.text: people and the others, then, from the mere lustful trembling of their loins,

36.text: they all died instantly.² This episode is repeated in many other tales. Some

37.text: of the old men complained to me that this extreme sensuality has developed

38.text: through the influence of modern times. “The people are spoiled,” said these
